item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Liberal Party calls for 'urgent' exemption clause to stop teen deportations, Norrlandsströmming herring gets EU protected origin status, and other news from Sweden on Tuesday.

item.title: Swedish government tells Migration Agency 'limited need' for work permit exemptions
item.description: Sweden's government has asked the Migration Agency to start from the premise that "the need for exemptions is limited" when drawing up its list of professions that should be excused the new higher salary threshold for a work permit when it comes into force in June.

item.title: UPDATED: What's the current status of Sweden's planned migration laws?
item.description: There are a number of migration-related laws and policies in the pipeline in Sweden, including changes to work permits, citizenship and permanent residency requirements, and plans to tighten up permanent residency and asylum applications.

item.title: TELL US: Do Sweden's new citizenship rules make you want to leave the country?
item.description: Sweden's government has announced that it will push ahead with plans to increase the residency requirement for citizenship from five years to eight, with the new rules applying retroactively. We want to hear whether they are changing readers' plans.

item.title: The battle to end Sweden's teen deportations
item.description: This week’s episode of Sweden in Focus Extra features interviews with the migration policy spokespeople from the Green and Centre parties.

item.title: How are children affected by Sweden's proposed stricter citizenship law?
item.description: An inquiry into stricter citizenship laws proposed ending citizenship for notification for most children, bringing in a requirement for good conduct and language and civics knowledge. Will those proposals be part of Sweden's new citizenship law?

item.title: What we know about Sweden’s new self-sufficiency requirement for citizenship
item.description: Sweden’s government has revealed more details about its plans to tighten up citizenship rules, including introducing a self-sufficiency requirement for citizenship applicants. Here’s what we know so far.

item.title: 'Collective punishment': Reader views on Sweden's stricter citizenship rules
item.description: Comments by readers of The Local Sweden ‒ whether opinions, advice, or tales of life in the country ‒ offer vital insights to others. We've picked out some recent contributions on Sweden's move to drastically toughen citizenship requirements.

item.title: Sweden's language requirement to be enforced from June 6th despite test delay
item.description: The new language and civics requirements for Swedish citizenship will start to apply from June 6th, even though the official tests will not be ready. Applicants will be required to prove their ability in other ways, the government has confirmed.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: PM says government 'will not freeze teen deportations', government and SD split on revoking permanent residency, and more news from Sweden on Wednesday.
